verification.method: scripts/verify/edu-115.py reads the original World Bank zips (data/raw/wdi/), not the site's generated data; check-wdi.mjs compares all generated WDI values with the original files; then the text was read by hand
verification.what: every ranking row (184 countries and areas: order, value and year of each country's latest figure from 2020), the CSV, every figure in the text, FAQ, title, description and JSON-LD; claims: median 4.2% (our calculation) with 101 at 4% or more, high- and low-income medians for 2022, Kiribati, Tuvalu, Micronesia highest, Somalia effectively zero then Nigeria, Zimbabwe, Papua New Guinea, Bangladesh 2.0% (2024) 167th and never above 2.7% since 2000, US 5.4% and UK 5.9% (2021); the World Bank world figure is a median and is not quoted as an average
verification.against: World Bank WDI bulk files and indicator metadata (update 11 November 2026, CC BY 4.0; data from the UNESCO Institute for Statistics)
verification.result: Before publishing, 'In South Asia, Pakistan' was corrected (the World Bank places Pakistan in its Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan region). All automated comparisons matched

changelog.note: First version: UNESCO government education spending (% of GDP) via World Bank WDI, latest year from 2020.
